subject: Specification of Informative Priors for Categorical Data in INLA

messages.author: 96e275f43eafb053
messages.subject: Specification of Informative Priors for Categorical Data in INLA
parts:
Hi All,

I am trying to fit a model which uses informative priors from historical data.
My concern is if I am specifying the categorical variables informative priors correctly
 I assumes that reference level from the model 1 of the historical data ie "A" follows a normal distribution with mean 0 and precision 0.001.
This makes reference level assumes uninformative prior contradicting my main purpose of using informative prior.
Here are some simulated data and code which shows my approach.
I will greatly apprecite any suggestions

require(INLA)

#data 1 (Historical data)
y<-rep(0:1, times=90)
x1<-rnorm(90,0.5,1)
x2<-as.factor(rep(c("A","B","C"),times=30))

data1<-data.frame(y=y,x1=x1,x2=x2)
head(data1)
attributes(data1$y)
#data 2 (Current Data)

y<-rep(0:1, times=15)
x1<-rnorm(30,0.4,0.2)
x2<-as.factor(rep(c("A","B", "C"),times=10))
data2<- data.frame(y=y,x1=x1,x2=x2)

#Model 1
model1<-inla(y~x1+x2,'binomial',control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
                 data=data1, control.family=list(link='logit'),
             control.fixed=list(mean=c(0,0,0,0),prec=c(0.001,0.001,0.001,0.001),
                                mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept=0.001))
summary(model1)

#Using uninformative priors N(0,1/sigma2)
model2<-inla(y~x1+x2,'binomial',control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
              data=data2, control.family=list(link='logit'),
              control.fixed=list(mean=c(0,0,0,0),prec=c(0.001,0.001,0.001,0.001),
                                  + mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept=0.001))
summary(model2)

#Using informartive priors from fixed effects 'mean' and 'SD'

model3<-inla(y~x1+x2,'binomial',control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
             data=data2, control.family=list(link='logit'),
             control.fixed=list(mean=c(-0.2186,1,-0.0237,-0.0237,0.0051),prec=c(13.42743,1,49.24592,7.465138),
                                mean.intercept=0.1142,prec.intercept=3.67242))
summary(model3)

Many thanks,
KE

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Specification of Informative Priors for Categorical Data in INLA
parts:
Hi,
You have four regression coefficients:
- Intercept: mean when x1=0 and x2=A
- a coefficient for the continuous covariate
- two coefficients for the categorical covariate: that is for x2=B and
X2=C

So, your code for model1 include
control.fixed=list(mean=c(0,0,0),prec=c(0.001,0.001,0.001),
mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept=0.001))
instead of length four mean and prec you considered.

You can see prior and posterior together with
plot(model2, plot.prior=TRUE)

Elias

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Specification of Informative Priors for Categorical Data in INLA
parts:
maybe its better to use a named list, to make it more explicite,
like

r = inla(y ~ a + b, data = data.frame(y=0,a=1,b=2), control.fixed =
list(mean=list(a=11,b=22)), verbose=TRUE)

and the same for 'precision'. you can use 'list(..., default=..) to
give default values not mentioned in the list

if you look at the output, you'll see like

section=[5] name=[b] type=[LINEAR]
inla_parse_linear...
section[b]
prior mean=[22]
prior precision=[0.001]


that you get the prior right. 

H
